---
title: "Random-effect distributions"
---

> **Maturity: experimental** — see [Feature Maturity](../maturity.qmd) for what this means.

By default every ETA is Gaussian, `η ~ N(0, Ω)`. A `density` clause on its
`omega` line gives it another distribution instead
([#1716](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1716)):

```
[parameters]
  theta TVCL(4.0, 0.1, 100.0)
  theta TVF(0.6, 0.01, 0.99)
  theta NU(10.0, 2.5, 100.0)
  omega ETA_CL ~ 0.09 density gamma
  omega ETA_F  ~ 0.02 density beta(TVF)
  omega ETA_V  ~ 0.06 density t(NU)

[individual_parameters]
  CL = TVCL * ETA_CL      # Gamma-distributed clearance, mean TVCL
  F  = ETA_F              # Beta-distributed bioavailability, mean TVF
  V  = TVV * exp(ETA_V)   # heavy-tailed log volume
```

As in Pumas's `@random` block, the ETA *is* the distributed quantity: under
`density gamma`, `ETA_CL` is a positive random variable with mean 1, so
`CL = TVCL * ETA_CL` has mean `TVCL` exactly. There is none of the mean bias of
`TVCL * exp(η)` or of a logit-normal fraction.

## Distributions

| `density` | support | mean | spread | shape θ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `t(ν)` | ℝ | 0 | scale² ω (variance `ω·ν/(ν−2)`) | ν, bounded above 0 |
| `logistic` | ℝ | 0 | variance ω | — |
| `gamma` | (0, ∞) | 1 | variance ω | — |
| `invgamma` | (0, ∞) | 1 | variance ω | — |
| `lognormal` | (0, ∞) | 1 | variance ω | — |
| `beta(μ)` | (0, 1) | μ | variance ω (needs ω < μ(1 − μ)) | μ, bounded in [0, 1] |
| `logitnormal(μ)` | (0, 1) | — | `logit η ~ N(logit μ, ω)` | μ, bounded in [0, 1] |

The value on the `omega` line is always ω. A shape θ is named inside the
parentheses, or declared automatically by empty ones: `density t()` declares
`NU_ETA_V` (init 80, bounds 3–100) and `density beta()` declares `MU_ETA_F`
(init 0.5, bounds 0.001–0.999).

A `block_omega` can carry `density t(ν)`, which makes the block a multivariate
t with one ν. The other kinds are univariate, and a block of them is refused:
correlating them needs a copula, which is not supported.

## Transforms

`transform KIND(SHAPE)` is the other form: η stays `N(0, ω)` and the model reads
`h(η)` wherever it reads the ETA. It is exactly the
[`[eta_shape]` block](eta-shape.qmd):

```
  omega ETA_CL ~ 0.09 transform boxcox(LAMBDA)
```

is `ETA_CL ~ boxcox(LAMBDA)` in `[eta_shape]`. `density boxcox(λ)` means the
same: on its latent scale the Box-Cox density is the Box-Cox transform, so the
two spellings are one model.

## How it is estimated

The estimators work on an unconstrained **latent** `z` for each density ETA,
and the model reads the random effect `m(z)`. The map is the identity on ℝ,
`exp` on (0, ∞) and `inv_logit` on (0, 1). The parser applies it to every read
of the ETA in `[individual_parameters]`. The prior is the exact latent density
`p_z(z) = p_η(m(z))·|m′(z)|`. So a constrained effect never leaves its support,
and the Laplace and FOCE machinery runs where the posterior is smooth.

Pumas maps a constrained random effect the same way. The ETA columns of the
sdtab and the EBEs report `z`, so for `gamma` the effect itself is `exp(ETA)`.

The prior's value, gradient and Hessian are exact, from dual numbers over one
implementation. That makes the FOCEI and Laplace adjoint gradients exact too,
including `∂/∂ω` and `∂/∂ν` / `∂/∂μ`.

- **FOCEI / Laplace / AGQ**: the conditional objective, with the density's
  curvature in `H̃`.
- **FOCE** (no interaction): the Sheiner–Beal marginal integrates η as a
  Gaussian, so a density model takes the conditional form FOCE uses beside a
  non-Gaussian endpoint (variance at the EBE, no interaction term). On a
  Gaussian model it is unchanged.
- **IMP / IMPMAP**: importance weights use the exact prior; the Gaussian
  defensive proposal stays a proposal.
- **SAEM / MCEM**: a density group's ω and shape θ have no sufficient
  statistic, so they move by Fisher scoring on their exact score, one step per
  SAEM iteration (NONMEM's rule for such parameters) and to convergence per
  MCEM iteration. Gaussian ETAs keep their closed form.
- **Bayes**: the η and θ moves score the exact prior (so ν and μ are sampled
  against it). A density ETA's ω has no conjugate update, so it moves by a
  Metropolis step on `ln ω` under the same inverse-gamma prior a Gaussian
  variance gets.
- **VI**: the KL term is sampled with the exact prior, and after each iteration
  a density group's ω and shape θ maximise the prior half of the ELBO over the
  variational draws (the MCEM objective).
- **Simulation** draws each kind from its own distribution.

A density ETA is not mu-referenced, and its omega row is labelled `custom`, with
no CV%.

### Not supported yet

A `[mixture]`, FREM, FOCE without interaction on a correlated residual
(`block_sigma`, `correlation`), a multivariate t block under `method = bayes`,
and `vi_omega_update = adam` are refused with `E_DENSITY_UNSUPPORTED`. An IOV
`kappa` cannot carry a `density`
([#1717](https://github.com/FeRx-NLME/ferx-core/issues/1717)).

## Validation

NONMEM has no non-Gaussian random-effect prior, so there is no NONMEM run to
anchor against. The checks are:

- **Closed forms and quadrature.** Each latent density integrates to 1, the
  random effect has the documented mean and variance (quadrature to 3e-14), the
  bivariate t matches the textbook log-density, and the gradients and Hessians
  match their hand-derived closed forms.
- **Reduction to an anchored model.** A `logitnormal(μ)` density is a Gaussian
  translated by `logit μ`, so its FOCEI objective and adjoint gradient equal the
  Gaussian model `inv_logit(logit(MU) + ETA)`, to 1e-15.
- **One objective.** The adjoint kernel's objective is the production
  objective exactly, and its inner gradient vanishes at production's EBE.
